Flex-start VM limited run duration
When you create a Flex-start VM, you must specify the following:
The VM run duration: you must specify how long the VMs can run. The run
duration can be up to seven days. If your workload completes before the VMs'
run duration ends, then you can stop or delete the standalone VMs, or delete
the VMs in a MIG to avoid unnecessary costs.
The VM termination action: you must choose whether
Compute Engine automatically stops or deletes the VMs at the end of
their run duration. For Flex-start VMs in a MIG, you can only
specify to delete VMs at the end of their run duration.
Caution: After Compute Engine stops a VM, you keep incurring charges
for any resources that are attached to the VM, such as disks or IP
addresses. To avoid unnecessary costs, detach and delete any resources that
you no longer need, or delete the VM. For more information, see the
pricing for a VM's uptime.

Pricing
For Flex-start VMs, you pay as you go (PAYG). For more
information, see
DWS pricing.

Persistent Disk and Hyperdisk pricing
Standard, SSD, and balanced Persistent Disks are priced by the amount of provisioned space per disk. For these disk types, I/O operations are included in the price for provisioned space. Since disk performance grows linearly with the size of your disk, consider your I/O needs when choosing the size of your disk.
You are billed for the total provisioned capacity of your Hyperdisk volumes until you delete them. You are charged per GiB per month. Additionally, you are billed for the following:
Hyperdisk Balanced and Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability charge a monthly rate for the provisioned IOPS and provisioned throughput (in MBps) in excess of the baseline values of 3,000 IOPS and 140 MBps throughput.
Hyperdisk Extreme charges a monthly rate based on the provisioned IOPS.
Hyperdisk Throughput charges a monthly rate based on the provisioned throughput (in MBps).

Public NAT
For Public NAT, the total cost for running a NAT gateway and running traffic through it includes the hourly cost for the NAT gateway plus all the following additional costs:
The cost per GiB of data that is processed by the gateway
The hourly cost for the external IP addresses used by the gateway
The data transfer out costs for any traffic leaving the network
Public NAT pricing is based on the following usage:
An hourly price for the NAT gateway that is based on the number of virtual machine (VM) instances that are using the gateway. The per-hour rate is capped at 32 VM instances. Gateways that are serving instances beyond the maximum number are charged at the maximum per-hour rate.
Google Cloud counts VM instances that get a NAT assignment as using the gateway. The NAT gateway performs source NAT (SNAT) for data transfer traffic from resources that don't have external IP addresses, and destination NAT (DNAT) for ingress packets that arrive as responses to outbound packets.
A per-GiB cost for data transfer that is processed by the gateway. The data processing price is the same across all regions. Data transfer costs to send traffic from the VM out of the network also apply.
An hourly price for each static or ephemeral external IP address that is used by a NAT gateway.

Flex-start and Calendar Mode prices are scheduled to be updated in November 2026.
Dynamic Workload Scheduler pricing
Dynamic Workload Scheduler (DWS) is a resource management and capacity scheduling platform designed for AI Hypercomputer. Dynamic Workload Scheduler provides a cost optimized consumption option for Google Cloud TPUs and NVIDIA GPUs. Dynamic Workload Scheduler is also integrated in many of your preferred Google Cloud AI/ML services: Compute Engine Managed Instance Groups, Google Kubernetes Engine, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Batch, and more.
Learn about Flex-start
Learn about Calendar mode
How DWS pricing works
DWS is variably priced and prices are updated periodically. You pay the price that is in effect when your instances are running. To compare DWS prices to on-demand and commitment rates, visit the Compute Engine pricing page.
Prices listed are exclusive of applicable taxes and duties, and do not reflect any enterprise negotiated pricing. To view your account’s specific pricing history, you can export your Cloud Billing data to BigQuery.
Pricing components
Dynamic Workload Scheduler Flex-start VMs are charged based on usage, in the same way as on-demand instances. A bill is sent out at the end of each billing cycle, providing a sum of Google Cloud charges. Calendar mode VMs are tied to a reservation in which you pay for the full duration the VMs are reserved for. Prices on this page are listed in U.S. dollars (USD). Disk size and machine type memory are listed in gigabytes (GB), where 1 GB is 2^30 bytes.

Default size, IOPS, and throughput values
If you don't specify a size, IOPS, or throughput value when you create a Hyperdisk Balanced
volume, Compute Engine assigns default values.
The default size for Hyperdisk Balanced volumes is 100 GiB.
The default IOPS and throughput are based on the following formulas, where
x is the volume's size in GiB.
Default IOPS:
Volumes 6 GiB or less: 500xIOPS
Volumes between 6 GiB and 26.666667 TiB: 6x + 3,000
IOPS
Volumes larger than 26.666667 TiB: 160,000 IOPS
Default throughput:
Volumes 6 GiB or less: 140 MiB/s
Volumes larger than 6 GiB: MIN (2,400, (1.5x + 140)) MiB/s
Important: A Hyperdisk volume
can't reach its provisioned performance unless you attach it to a compute instance
that supports that level of performance, or higher. For detailed performance
limits for all supported instances by machine type, see
Performance limits when attached to an instance.
Baseline performance
Hyperdisk Balanced volumes include baseline, or free performance. The first 3,000 IOPS and
140 MiB/s of throughput that you provision for a volume are free.
Performance you provision
above the baseline amounts is billable performance,
and is not free. If you provision a volume with 5,000 IOPS, you're billed for
2,000 IOPS. Similar principles apply to throughput.

Provisioning model: Flex-start.
Broad hardware support: request any clustered GPU
machine type, except A4X Max and A4X.
Latency optimization: apply a compact placement policy to standalone VMs to
minimize network latency.
Cost efficiency: receive a discount of up to 53% on vCPUs, memory, GPUs,
and Local SSD disks for A4, A3, A2, and G4 machine series. Standard on-demand rates apply to
other supported series. For more information, see Flex-start pricing.

[mappings.machine]
service        = "Compute Engine"
product_family = "Compute Instance"
attribute_filters = [
  { key = "machineType", expr = 'default(machine_type, "e2-medium")' },
]

[mappings.boot_disk]
service        = "Compute Engine"
product_family = "Storage"
attribute_filters = [
  { key = "description", expr = '''
      default(boot_disk_initialize_params_type, "pd-standard") == "pd-ssd" ? "SSD backed PD Capacity" :
      default(boot_disk_initialize_params_type, "pd-standard") == "pd-balanced" ? "Balanced PD Capacity" :
                                                                                  "Storage PD Capacity"
  ''' },
]

[mappings.gpu]
service        = "Compute Engine"
product_family = "Compute"
attribute_filters = [
  { key = "description", expr = '''
      default(guest_accelerator_type, "nvidia-tesla-t4") == "nvidia-l4" ?
        "Nvidia L4 GPU running in Americas" :
        "Nvidia Tesla T4 GPU running in Americas"
  ''' },
]

[[dimensions]]
id       = "compute"
label    = "Instance (on-demand)"
unit     = "hours"
when     = '!(default(machine_type, "e2-medium") startsWith "custom")'
quantity = "monthly_hours()"
rate     = 'price("machine")'

[[dimensions]]
id       = "custom_vcpu"

when     = 'default(machine_type, "e2-medium") startsWith "custom"'
quantity = "default(vcpu_count, 2) * monthly_hours()"
rate     = 'price("custom_core")'

label    = "Custom machine RAM"
unit     = "GiB-hours"
when     = 'default(machine_type, "e2-medium") startsWith "custom"'
quantity = "default(memory_gb, 4) * monthly_hours()"
rate     = 'price("custom_ram")'

[[dimensions]]

[[dimensions]]

func DefaultPurchaseOption(provider string) string {
	switch provider {
	case "aws":
		return "on_demand"
	case "azure":
		return "Consumption"
	case "gcp":
		return "OnDemand"
	default:
		return ""
	}
